body:
GREG, 2026-11-08 about 02:44Z, relayed by Engram::Asistant (mailbox 43498a6e #655, message f827a7ee). Verbatim: „wazne aby nie laczyc taskow/evidence z kodem, bo to stanowi duzy problem”.
Asistant's relay of the rest (a paraphrase, not verbatim):
- Greg proposes a separate branch for task data, and considering separate MONTHLY evidence branches to allow retention later. The retention policy can come later.
- He asks Kimi and the Engram team to analyse this together and adapt the design before implementation: simple exchange of task text and full results through Git, without TermAl.
- To consider: independence of month histories; real limits of Git deletion and clones; concurrent changes; impact on the sync work already started.
- The monthly split is a proposal to evaluate, not an imposed detail.
- He wants a joint concrete conclusion and its consequences for the work, with no extra approval gate.
This changes the current design in docs/features/git-task-sync.md and AGENTS (task text on the ordinary code branch, gated with the code changeset). Any instruction change that grants agents a new push (for example to a data branch) still follows the AGENTS rule for authority text (both coordinators, Greg sent the exact wording, final-diff audit; a widening needs Greg's recorded word on that widening).
